<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">    req.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">on</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'data'</span><span style="color:#24292E">, </span><span style="color:#E36209">chunk</span><span style="color:#D73A49"> =&gt;</span><span style="color:#24292E"> {</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">      body </span><span style="color:#D73A49">+=</span><span style="color:#24292E"> chunk.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">toString</span><span style="color:#24292E">(); </span><span style="color:#6A737D">// Collect data chunks from the request body</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">    });</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">    req.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">on</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'end'</span><span style="color:#24292E">, () </span><span style="color:#D73A49">=&gt;</span><span style="color:#24292E"> {</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#D73A49">      const</span><span style="color:#005CC5"> formData</span><span style="color:#D73A49"> =</span><span style="color:#24292E"> querystring.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">parse</span><span style="color:#24292E">(body); </span><span style="color:#6A737D">// Parse the URL-encoded form data</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">      console.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">log</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'Form submitted with data:'</span><span style="color:#24292E">, formData);</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">      // In a real application, you would save this data to a database.</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">      // For this example, we just acknowledge receipt.</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">      res.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">writeHead</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#005CC5">200</span><span style="color:#24292E">, { </span><span style="color:#032F62">'Content-Type'</span><span style="color:#24292E">: </span><span style="color:#032F62">'text/html'</span><span style="color:#24292E"> });</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">      res.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">end</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">`</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#032F62">        &lt;!DOCTYPE html&gt;</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#032F62">        &lt;html lang="en"&gt;</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#032F62">        &lt;head&gt;</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#032F62">            &lt;meta charset="UTF-8"&gt;</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#032F62">            &lt;meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0"&gt;</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#032F62">            &lt;title&gt;Submission Success&lt;/title&gt;</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#032F62">        &lt;/head&gt;</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#032F62">        &lt;body&gt;</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#032F62">            &lt;h1&gt;Item Submitted Successfully!&lt;/h1&gt;</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#032F62">            &lt;p&gt;You submitted: &lt;strong&gt;${</span><span style="color:#24292E">formData</span><span style="color:#032F62">.</span><span style="color:#24292E">itemName</span><span style="color:#032F62">}&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#032F62">            &lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="/"&gt;Go back to homepage&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#032F62">        &lt;/body&gt;</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#032F62">        &lt;/html&gt;</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#032F62">      `</span><span style="color:#24292E">);</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">    });</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">  } </span><span style="color:#D73A49">else</span><span style="color:#24292E"> {</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">    // Handle 404 for any other path or method</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">    res.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">writeHead</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#005CC5">404</span><span style="color:#24292E">, { </span><span style="color:#032F62">'Content-Type'</span><span style="color:#24292E">: </span><span style="color:#032F62">'text/html'</span><span style="color:#24292E"> });</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">    res.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">end</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'&lt;h1&gt;404 Not Found&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;p&gt;The requested page could not be found.&lt;/p&gt;'</span><span style="color:#24292E">);</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">  }</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">});</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#D73A49">const</span><span style="color:#005CC5"> PORT</span><span style="color:#D73A49"> =</span><span style="color:#005CC5"> 3000</span><span style="color:#24292E">;</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">server.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">listen</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#005CC5">PORT</span><span style="color:#24292E">, () </span><span style="color:#D73A49">=&gt;</span><span style="color:#24292E"> {</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">  console.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">log</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">`Server running at http://localhost:${</span><span style="color:#005CC5">PORT</span><span style="color:#032F62">}/`</span><span style="color:#24292E">);</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">});</span></span></code></pre></div></div></div>
<p>To run this example:</p>
<ol>
<li>Save the code as <code>app.js</code>.</li>
<li>Run <code>node app.js</code> in your terminal.</li>
<li>Open <code>http://localhost:3000/</code> in your browser. You will see the homepage with a form.</li>
<li>Navigate to <code>http://localhost:3000/api/products</code> to see the JSON output.</li>
<li>Submit the form on the homepage. The server will process the POST request and display a success message.</li>
</ol>
<h2>Exercises</h2>
<p>These exercises build on the concepts of creating a basic Node.js server, routing, and handling different request types.</p>
<h3>Exercise 1: Extend the Product API</h3>
<p>Modify the <code>app.js</code> server to include a new API endpoint for a single product.</p>
<p><strong>Task:</strong></p>
<ol>
<li>Add a route <code>GET /api/products/:id</code> where <code>:id</code> is a product ID.</li>
<li>When a request comes to this route, parse the <code>id</code> from the URL.</li>
<li>If a product with the matching <code>id</code> is found in the <code>products</code> array, respond with that product's JSON data.</li>
<li>If no product is found, respond with a 404 status code and a JSON error message.</li>
</ol>
<p><strong>Hints:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>You will need to parse the <code>path</code> to extract the <code>id</code>. A simple way for this exercise is to split the path string. For example, <code>path.split('/')</code> will give you an array like <code>['', 'api', 'products', '1']</code>.</li>
<li>Remember <code>parseInt()</code> to convert the ID string to a number for comparison.</li>
</ul>
<h3>Exercise 2: Create a Static File Server Segment</h3>
<p>Modify the <code>app.js</code> server to serve a simple static CSS file.</p>
<p><strong>Task:</strong></p>
<ol>
<li>Create a new directory named <code>public</code> in your project root.</li>
<li>Inside <code>public</code>, create a file <code>style.css</code> with some basic CSS (e.g., <code>body { font-family: sans-serif; background-color: #f0f0f0; }</code>).</li>
<li>Modify the HTML served at the root route (<code>/</code>) to link to this <code>style.css</code> file.</li>
<li>Add a new route <code>GET /style.css</code> to your server.</li>
<li>When <code>GET /style.css</code> is requested, read the <code>style.css</code> file from the <code>public</code> directory and send its content as the response, setting the <code>Content-Type</code> header to <code>text/css</code>.</li>
</ol>
<p><strong>Hints:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>You will need the built-in Node.js <code>fs</code> (file system) module to read files. <code>const fs = require('fs');</code></li>
<li>Use <code>fs.readFile()</code> or <code>fs.readFileSync()</code> to read the file.</li>
<li>Be mindful of asynchronous operations if using <code>fs.readFile()</code>. For this simple exercise, <code>fs.readFileSync()</code> can be used for synchronous file reading.</li>
</ul>
<h3>Exercise 3: User Feedback Endpoint</h3>
<p>Add a new endpoint to handle user feedback.</p>
<p><strong>Task:</strong></p>
<ol>
<li>Create a new HTML page for feedback submission at <code>GET /feedback</code>. This page should contain a simple form with a text area for feedback and a submit button, posting to <code>POST /submit-feedback</code>.</li>
<li>Implement the <code>POST /submit-feedback</code> endpoint.</li>
<li>When a POST request arrives at <code>/submit-feedback</code>, extract the feedback text from the request body.</li>
<li>Log the feedback to the server console.</li>
<li>Send a success HTML response back to the user, confirming their feedback was received.</li>
</ol>
<p><strong>Hints:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Remember to collect the request body chunks for POST requests.</li>
<li>Use <code>querystring.parse()</code> if the form submits <code>application/x-www-form-urlencoded</code> data.</li>
</ul>
  
</div>

<div id="chapter-6.3">

<h1 class="mb-6 text-3xl font-semibold text-balance max-lg:mb-3 max-lg:text-xl">Introduction to Express.js: Routing and Middleware</h1><p>Express.js is a minimalist web framework for Node.js that simplifies the process of building web applications and APIs. It provides a robust set of features for web and mobile applications, including routing, middleware, template engines, and more. This lesson focuses on understanding the core concepts of Express.js: routing, which defines how an application responds to client requests to specific endpoints, and middleware, which are functions that have access to the request and response objects and can perform tasks like logging, authentication, or data parsing.</p>
<h2>Initializing an Express Application</h2>
<p>To begin using Express.js, it must first be installed as a dependency in a Node.js project. After installation, an Express application instance can be created, which serves as the foundation for defining routes and middleware.</p>
<p>First, initialize a Node.js project:</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6 max-w-full overflow-hidden rounded-lg border border-gray-200 has-[code:empty]:hidden"><div class="flex items-center justify-between gap-2 border-b border-gray-200 bg-gray-50 px-3 py-2"><span class="text-sm text-gray-600">bash</span><div class="flex items-center gap-2"><button class="flex size-6 items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-md text-gray-400 hover:bg-zinc-200 hover:text-black focus:outline-none"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy size-3.5" aria-hidden="true"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"></rect><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"></path></svg></button></div></div><div class="mt-0 text-sm [&amp;_pre]:py-0 [&amp;_pre]:grid [&amp;_code]:py-4 [&amp;_code]:w-full [&amp;_code]:grid [&amp;_code]:overflow-x-auto [&amp;_code]:no-scrollbar [&amp;_code]:bg-transparent [&amp;_.line]:px-3 [&amp;_.line]:w-full [&amp;_.line]:relative [&amp;_.line]:min-h-5"><div><pre class="shiki github-light" style="background-color:#fff;color:#24292e" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#6F42C1">npm</span><span style="color:#032F62"> init</span><span style="color:#005CC5"> -y</span></span></code></pre></div></div></div>
<p>Then, install Express:</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6 max-w-full overflow-hidden rounded-lg border border-gray-200 has-[code:empty]:hidden"><div class="flex items-center justify-between gap-2 border-b border-gray-200 bg-gray-50 px-3 py-2"><span class="text-sm text-gray-600">bash</span><div class="flex items-center gap-2"><button class="flex size-6 items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-md text-gray-400 hover:bg-zinc-200 hover:text-black focus:outline-none"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy size-3.5" aria-hidden="true"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"></rect><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"></path></svg></button></div></div><div class="mt-0 text-sm [&amp;_pre]:py-0 [&amp;_pre]:grid [&amp;_code]:py-4 [&amp;_code]:w-full [&amp;_code]:grid [&amp;_code]:overflow-x-auto [&amp;_code]:no-scrollbar [&amp;_code]:bg-transparent [&amp;_.line]:px-3 [&amp;_.line]:w-full [&amp;_.line]:relative [&amp;_.line]:min-h-5"><div><pre class="shiki github-light" style="background-color:#fff;color:#24292e" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#6F42C1">npm</span><span style="color:#032F62"> install</span><span style="color:#032F62"> express</span></span></code></pre></div></div></div>
<p>Now, create a basic Express application:</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6 max-w-full overflow-hidden rounded-lg border border-gray-200 has-[code:empty]:hidden"><div class="flex items-center justify-between gap-2 border-b border-gray-200 bg-gray-50 px-3 py-2"><span class="text-sm text-gray-600">javascript</span><div class="flex items-center gap-2"><button class="flex size-6 items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-md text-gray-400 hover:bg-zinc-200 hover:text-black focus:outline-none"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy size-3.5" aria-hidden="true"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"></rect><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"></path></svg></button></div></div><div class="mt-0 text-sm [&amp;_pre]:py-0 [&amp;_pre]:grid [&amp;_code]:py-4 [&amp;_code]:w-full [&amp;_code]:grid [&amp;_code]:overflow-x-auto [&amp;_code]:no-scrollbar [&amp;_code]:bg-transparent [&amp;_.line]:px-3 [&amp;_.line]:w-full [&amp;_.line]:relative [&amp;_.line]:min-h-5"><div><pre class="shiki github-light" style="background-color:#fff;color:#24292e" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// app.js</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#D73A49">const</span><span style="color:#005CC5"> express</span><span style="color:#D73A49"> =</span><span style="color:#6F42C1"> require</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'express'</span><span style="color:#24292E">); </span><span style="color:#6A737D">// Import the Express module</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#D73A49">const</span><span style="color:#005CC5"> app</span><span style="color:#D73A49"> =</span><span style="color:#6F42C1"> express</span><span style="color:#24292E">();              </span><span style="color:#6A737D">// Create an Express application instance</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#D73A49">const</span><span style="color:#005CC5"> port</span><span style="color:#D73A49"> =</span><span style="color:#005CC5"> 3000</span><span style="color:#24292E">;                  </span><span style="color:#6A737D">// Define the port for the server</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// Start the server and listen on the defined port</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">app.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">listen</span><span style="color:#24292E">(port, () </span><span style="color:#D73A49">=&gt;</span><span style="color:#24292E"> {</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">  console.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">log</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">`Server listening at http://localhost:${</span><span style="color:#24292E">port</span><span style="color:#032F62">}`</span><span style="color:#24292E">);</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">});</span></span></code></pre></div></div></div>
<p>To run this application, execute <code>node app.js</code> in your terminal. This will start a server, but it won't respond to any requests yet, as no routes have been defined.</p>
<h2>Routing</h2>
<p>Routing determines how a web application responds to a client request for a particular endpoint, which is a URI (or path) and a specific HTTP request method (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, etc.). Each route can have one or more handler functions, which are executed when the route is matched.</p>
<h3>Defining Basic Routes</h3>
<p>Express provides methods for each HTTP verb (e.g., <code>app.get()</code>, <code>app.post()</code>, <code>app.put()</code>, <code>app.delete()</code>) to define routes. These methods take two arguments: the path and a callback function (the route handler). The route handler function receives <code>request</code> (<code>req</code>) and <code>response</code> (<code>res</code>) objects as arguments.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6 max-w-full overflow-hidden rounded-lg border border-gray-200 has-[code:empty]:hidden"><div class="flex items-center justify-between gap-2 border-b border-gray-200 bg-gray-50 px-3 py-2"><span class="text-sm text-gray-600">javascript</span><div class="flex items-center gap-2"><button class="flex size-6 items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-md text-gray-400 hover:bg-zinc-200 hover:text-black focus:outline-none"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy size-3.5" aria-hidden="true"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"></rect><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"></path></svg></button></div></div><div class="mt-0 text-sm [&amp;_pre]:py-0 [&amp;_pre]:grid [&amp;_code]:py-4 [&amp;_code]:w-full [&amp;_code]:grid [&amp;_code]:overflow-x-auto [&amp;_code]:no-scrollbar [&amp;_code]:bg-transparent [&amp;_.line]:px-3 [&amp;_.line]:w-full [&amp;_.line]:relative [&amp;_.line]:min-h-5"><div><pre class="shiki github-light" style="background-color:#fff;color:#24292e" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// app.js (continuation)</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// ... (previous setup)</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// GET request to the root path '/'</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">app.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">get</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'/'</span><span style="color:#24292E">, (</span><span style="color:#E36209">req</span><span style="color:#24292E">, </span><span style="color:#E36209">res</span><span style="color:#24292E">) </span><span style="color:#D73A49">=&gt;</span><span style="color:#24292E"> {</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">  res.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">send</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'Welcome to the homepage!'</span><span style="color:#24292E">); </span><span style="color:#6A737D">// Send a simple text response</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">});</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// GET request to '/about'</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">app.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">get</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'/about'</span><span style="color:#24292E">, (</span><span style="color:#E36209">req</span><span style="color:#24292E">, </span><span style="color:#E36209">res</span><span style="color:#24292E">) </span><span style="color:#D73A49">=&gt;</span><span style="color:#24292E"> {</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">  res.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">send</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'This is the About Us page.'</span><span style="color:#24292E">);</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">});</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// GET request to '/contact'</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">app.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">get</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'/contact'</span><span style="color:#24292E">, (</span><span style="color:#E36209">req</span><span style="color:#24292E">, </span><span style="color:#E36209">res</span><span style="color:#24292E">) </span><span style="color:#D73A49">=&gt;</span><span style="color:#24292E"> {</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">  res.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">send</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'Reach us at contact@example.com'</span><span style="color:#24292E">);</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">});</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// ... (app.listen)</span></span></code></pre></div></div></div>
<p>If you run this <code>app.js</code> and visit <code>http://localhost:3000/</code> in your browser, you will see "Welcome to the homepage!". Navigating to <code>http://localhost:3000/about</code> will show "This is the About Us page.".</p>
<h3>Route Parameters</h3>
<p>Route parameters are named URL segments that are used to capture the values specified at their position in the URL. The captured values are stored in the <code>req.params</code> object.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6 max-w-full overflow-hidden rounded-lg border border-gray-200 has-[code:empty]:hidden"><div class="flex items-center justify-between gap-2 border-b border-gray-200 bg-gray-50 px-3 py-2"><span class="text-sm text-gray-600">javascript</span><div class="flex items-center gap-2"><button class="flex size-6 items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-md text-gray-400 hover:bg-zinc-200 hover:text-black focus:outline-none"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy size-3.5" aria-hidden="true"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"></rect><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"></path></svg></button></div></div><div class="mt-0 text-sm [&amp;_pre]:py-0 [&amp;_pre]:grid [&amp;_code]:py-4 [&amp;_code]:w-full [&amp;_code]:grid [&amp;_code]:overflow-x-auto [&amp;_code]:no-scrollbar [&amp;_code]:bg-transparent [&amp;_.line]:px-3 [&amp;_.line]:w-full [&amp;_.line]:relative [&amp;_.line]:min-h-5"><div><pre class="shiki github-light" style="background-color:#fff;color:#24292e" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// app.js (continuation)</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// ... (previous setup and basic routes)</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// GET request with a route parameter ':id'</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">app.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">get</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'/users/:id'</span><span style="color:#24292E">, (</span><span style="color:#E36209">req</span><span style="color:#24292E">, </span><span style="color:#E36209">res</span><span style="color:#24292E">) </span><span style="color:#D73A49">=&gt;</span><span style="color:#24292E"> {</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#D73A49">  const</span><span style="color:#005CC5"> userId</span><span style="color:#D73A49"> =</span><span style="color:#24292E"> req.params.id; </span><span style="color:#6A737D">// Access the 'id' parameter from req.params</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">  res.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">send</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">`User ID: ${</span><span style="color:#24292E">userId</span><span style="color:#032F62">}`</span><span style="color:#24292E">);</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">});</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// GET request with multiple route parameters</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">app.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">get</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'/products/:category/:productId'</span><span style="color:#24292E">, (</span><span style="color:#E36209">req</span><span style="color:#24292E">, </span><span style="color:#E36209">res</span><span style="color:#24292E">) </span><span style="color:#D73A49">=&gt;</span><span style="color:#24292E"> {</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#D73A49">  const</span><span style="color:#005CC5"> category</span><span style="color:#D73A49"> =</span><span style="color:#24292E"> req.params.category;</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#D73A49">  const</span><span style="color:#005CC5"> productId</span><span style="color:#D73A49"> =</span><span style="color:#24292E"> req.params.productId;</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">  res.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">send</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">`Category: ${</span><span style="color:#24292E">category</span><span style="color:#032F62">}, Product ID: ${</span><span style="color:#24292E">productId</span><span style="color:#032F62">}`</span><span style="color:#24292E">);</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">});</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// ... (app.listen)</span></span></code></pre></div></div></div>
<p>Visiting <code>http://localhost:3000/users/123</code> would respond with "User ID: 123". Visiting <code>http://localhost:3000/products/electronics/abc</code> would respond with "Category: electronics, Product ID: abc".</p>
<h3>Route Handlers</h3>
<p>A route can have multiple handler functions. When multiple handler functions are provided, they are executed in sequence, typically by calling <code>next()</code> to pass control to the next handler.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6 max-w-full overflow-hidden rounded-lg border border-gray-200 has-[code:empty]:hidden"><div class="flex items-center justify-between gap-2 border-b border-gray-200 bg-gray-50 px-3 py-2"><span class="text-sm text-gray-600">javascript</span><div class="flex items-center gap-2"><button class="flex size-6 items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-md text-gray-400 hover:bg-zinc-200 hover:text-black focus:outline-none"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy size-3.5" aria-hidden="true"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"></rect><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"></path></svg></button></div></div><div class="mt-0 text-sm [&amp;_pre]:py-0 [&amp;_pre]:grid [&amp;_code]:py-4 [&amp;_code]:w-full [&amp;_code]:grid [&amp;_code]:overflow-x-auto [&amp;_code]:no-scrollbar [&amp;_code]:bg-transparent [&amp;_.line]:px-3 [&amp;_.line]:w-full [&amp;_.line]:relative [&amp;_.line]:min-h-5"><div><pre class="shiki github-light" style="background-color:#fff;color:#24292e" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// app.js (continuation)</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// ... (previous setup and routes)</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// First handler function</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#D73A49">const</span><span style="color:#6F42C1"> loggerMiddleware</span><span style="color:#D73A49"> =</span><span style="color:#24292E"> (</span><span style="color:#E36209">req</span><span style="color:#24292E">, </span><span style="color:#E36209">res</span><span style="color:#24292E">, </span><span style="color:#E36209">next</span><span style="color:#24292E">) </span><span style="color:#D73A49">=&gt;</span><span style="color:#24292E"> {</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">  console.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">log</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'Request received at:'</span><span style="color:#24292E">, </span><span style="color:#D73A49">new</span><span style="color:#6F42C1"> Date</span><span style="color:#24292E">().</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">toISOString</span><span style="color:#24292E">());</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6F42C1">  next</span><span style="color:#24292E">(); </span><span style="color:#6A737D">// Pass control to the next handler</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">};</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// Second handler function</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#D73A49">const</span><span style="color:#6F42C1"> authMiddleware</span><span style="color:#D73A49"> =</span><span style="color:#24292E"> (</span><span style="color:#E36209">req</span><span style="color:#24292E">, </span><span style="color:#E36209">res</span><span style="color:#24292E">, </span><span style="color:#E36209">next</span><span style="color:#24292E">) </span><span style="color:#D73A49">=&gt;</span><span style="color:#24292E"> {</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">  // In a real app, this would check for authentication tokens</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#D73A49">  const</span><span style="color:#005CC5"> isAuthenticated</span><span style="color:#D73A49"> =</span><span style="color:#005CC5"> true</span><span style="color:#24292E">; </span><span style="color:#6A737D">// Simulate authentication</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#D73A49">  if</span><span style="color:#24292E"> (isAuthenticated) {</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">    console.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">log</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'User is authenticated.'</span><span style="color:#24292E">);</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">    req.user </span><span style="color:#D73A49">=</span><span style="color:#24292E"> { id: </span><span style="color:#005CC5">1</span><span style="color:#24292E">, name: </span><span style="color:#032F62">'John Doe'</span><span style="color:#24292E"> }; </span><span style="color:#6A737D">// Attach user info to the request object</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6F42C1">    next</span><span style="color:#24292E">(); </span><span style="color:#6A737D">// Pass control to the next handler</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">  } </span><span style="color:#D73A49">else</span><span style="color:#24292E"> {</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">    res.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">status</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#005CC5">401</span><span style="color:#24292E">).</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">send</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'Unauthorized'</span><span style="color:#24292E">);</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">  }</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">};</span></span>

<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// Route with multiple handler functions</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">app.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">get</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'/dashboard'</span><span style="color:#24292E">, loggerMiddleware, authMiddleware, (</span><span style="color:#E36209">req</span><span style="color:#24292E">, </span><span style="color:#E36209">res</span><span style="color:#24292E">) </span><span style="color:#D73A49">=&gt;</span><span style="color:#24292E"> {</span></span>

<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">});</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// ... (app.listen)</span></span></code></pre></div></div></div>
<p>When you access <code>http://localhost:3000/dashboard</code>, the <code>loggerMiddleware</code> runs, logs the time, then calls <code>next()</code>. Then <code>authMiddleware</code> runs, logs authentication status, attaches <code>req.user</code>, and calls <code>next()</code>. Finally, the route handler executes, responding with "Welcome to your dashboard, John Doe!". The console will show the log messages from the middleware functions.</p>
<h3>Handling All HTTP Methods</h3>
<p>The <code>app.all()</code> method can be used to handle all HTTP methods at a specific path. This is useful for applying logic regardless of the request method, such as authentication checks for all actions on a resource.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6 max-w-full overflow-hidden rounded-lg border border-gray-200 has-[code:empty]:hidden"><div class="flex items-center justify-between gap-2 border-b border-gray-200 bg-gray-50 px-3 py-2"><span class="text-sm text-gray-600">javascript</span><div class="flex items-center gap-2"><button class="flex size-6 items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-md text-gray-400 hover:bg-zinc-200 hover:text-black focus:outline-none"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy size-3.5" aria-hidden="true"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"></rect><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"></path></svg></button></div></div><div class="mt-0 text-sm [&amp;_pre]:py-0 [&amp;_pre]:grid [&amp;_code]:py-4 [&amp;_code]:w-full [&amp;_code]:grid [&amp;_code]:overflow-x-auto [&amp;_code]:no-scrollbar [&amp;_code]:bg-transparent [&amp;_.line]:px-3 [&amp;_.line]:w-full [&amp;_.line]:relative [&amp;_.line]:min-h-5"><div><pre class="shiki github-light" style="background-color:#fff;color:#24292e" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// app.js (continuation)</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// ... (previous setup and routes)</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">app.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">all</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'/secret'</span><span style="color:#24292E">, (</span><span style="color:#E36209">req</span><span style="color:#24292E">, </span><span style="color:#E36209">res</span><span style="color:#24292E">, </span><span style="color:#E36209">next</span><span style="color:#24292E">) </span><span style="color:#D73A49">=&gt;</span><span style="color:#24292E"> {</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">  console.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">log</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'Accessing the secret section...'</span><span style="color:#24292E">);</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6F42C1">  next</span><span style="color:#24292E">(); </span><span style="color:#6A737D">// Pass control to the next handler for the specific method</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">});</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">app.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">get</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'/secret'</span><span style="color:#24292E">, (</span><span style="color:#E36209">req</span><span style="color:#24292E">, </span><span style="color:#E36209">res</span><span style="color:#24292E">) </span><span style="color:#D73A49">=&gt;</span><span style="color:#24292E"> {</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">  res.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">send</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'Welcome to the secret GET page!'</span><span style="color:#24292E">);</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">});</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">app.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">post</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'/secret'</span><span style="color:#24292E">, (</span><span style="color:#E36209">req</span><span style="color:#24292E">, </span><span style="color:#E36209">res</span><span style="color:#24292E">) </span><span style="color:#D73A49">=&gt;</span><span style="color:#24292E"> {</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">  res.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">send</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'Welcome to the secret POST page!'</span><span style="color:#24292E">);</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">});</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// ... (app.listen)</span></span></code></pre></div></div></div>
<p>Whether you make a GET or POST request to <code>/secret</code>, the <code>app.all</code> handler will execute first, logging "Accessing the secret section...", before the specific GET or POST handler takes over.</p>
<h3>The <code>res</code> Object for Sending Responses</h3>
<p>The <code>res</code> object provides methods to send various types of responses to the client.</p>
<ul>
<li><code>res.send()</code>: Sends various types of responses (HTML, JSON, plain text, etc.). Express automatically sets the <code>Content-Type</code> header based on the argument.</li>
<li><code>res.json()</code>: Sends a JSON response. It automatically sets the <code>Content-Type</code> to <code>application/json</code>.</li>
<li><code>res.status()</code>: Sets the HTTP status code for the response. It can be chained with other response methods.</li>
<li><code>res.redirect()</code>: Redirects the client to a different URL.</li>
<li><code>res.sendFile()</code>: Sends a file from a specified path.</li>
</ul>

<li><code>http://localhost:3000/old-page</code> will automatically redirect to <code>http://localhost:3000/new-page</code>.</li>
</ul>
<h2>Middleware</h2>
<p>Middleware functions are functions that have access to the <code>request</code> object (<code>req</code>), the <code>response</code> object (<code>res</code>), and the <code>next</code> middleware function in the application’s request-response cycle. The <code>next</code> function is a function in the Express router that, when invoked, executes the next middleware function in the stack. Middleware can perform tasks like:</p>
<ul>
<li>Executing any code.</li>
<li>Making changes to the request and the response objects.</li>
<li>Ending the request-response cycle.</li>
<li>Calling the next middleware in the stack.</li>
</ul>
<h3>Types of Middleware</h3>
<ol>
<li><strong>Application-level middleware</strong>: Bound to an instance of the <code>app</code> object using <code>app.use()</code> and <code>app.METHOD()</code>.</li>
<li><strong>Router-level middleware</strong>: Bound to an instance of <code>express.Router()</code>.</li>
<li><strong>Error-handling middleware</strong>: Always takes four arguments: <code>(err, req, res, next)</code>.</li>
<li><strong>Built-in middleware</strong>: <code>express.static</code>, <code>express.json</code>, <code>express.urlencoded</code>.</li>
<li><strong>Third-party middleware</strong>: For specific tasks like <code>cookie-parser</code>, <code>cors</code>.</li>
</ol>
<h3>Application-Level Middleware</h3>
<p>Application-level middleware functions are executed for every request to the application, or for specific paths depending on how they are mounted.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6 max-w-full overflow-hidden rounded-lg border border-gray-200 has-[code:empty]:hidden"><div class="flex items-center justify-between gap-2 border-b border-gray-200 bg-gray-50 px-3 py-2"><span class="text-sm text-gray-600">javascript</span><div class="flex items-center gap-2"><button class="flex size-6 items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-md text-gray-400 hover:bg-zinc-200 hover:text-black focus:outline-none"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy size-3.5" aria-hidden="true"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"></rect><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"></path></svg></button></div></div><div class="mt-0 text-sm [&amp;_pre]:py-0 [&amp;_pre]:grid [&amp;_code]:py-4 [&amp;_code]:w-full [&amp;_code]:grid [&amp;_code]:overflow-x-auto [&amp;_code]:no-scrollbar [&amp;_code]:bg-transparent [&amp;_.line]:px-3 [&amp;_.line]:w-full [&amp;_.line]:relative [&amp;_.line]:min-h-5"><div><pre class="shiki github-light" style="background-color:#fff;color:#24292e" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// app.js (continuation)</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// ... (previous setup and routes)</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// Global logging middleware: this runs for *every* request</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">app.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">use</span><span style="color:#24292E">((</span><span style="color:#E36209">req</span><span style="color:#24292E">, </span><span style="color:#E36209">res</span><span style="color:#24292E">, </span><span style="color:#E36209">next</span><span style="color:#24292E">) </span><span style="color:#D73A49">=&gt;</span><span style="color:#24292E"> {</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">  console.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">log</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">`[${</span><span style="color:#D73A49">new</span><span style="color:#6F42C1"> Date</span><span style="color:#032F62">().</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">toLocaleString</span><span style="color:#032F62">()</span><span style="color:#032F62">}] ${</span><span style="color:#24292E">req</span><span style="color:#032F62">.</span><span style="color:#24292E">method</span><span style="color:#032F62">} ${</span><span style="color:#24292E">req</span><span style="color:#032F62">.</span><span style="color:#24292E">url</span><span style="color:#032F62">}`</span><span style="color:#24292E">);</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6F42C1">  next</span><span style="color:#24292E">(); </span><span style="color:#6A737D">// Crucial to call next() to pass control to the next middleware or route handler</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">});</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// Example of middleware specific to a path</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">app.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">use</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'/admin'</span><span style="color:#24292E">, (</span><span style="color:#E36209">req</span><span style="color:#24292E">, </span><span style="color:#E36209">res</span><span style="color:#24292E">, </span><span style="color:#E36209">next</span><span style="color:#24292E">) </span><span style="color:#D73A49">=&gt;</span><span style="color:#24292E"> {</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">  console.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">log</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'Accessing admin section...'</span><span style="color:#24292E">);</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">  // In a real application, check user roles, permissions etc.</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">  req.isAdmin </span><span style="color:#D73A49">=</span><span style="color:#005CC5"> true</span><span style="color:#24292E">; </span><span style="color:#6A737D">// Add a property to the request object</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6F42C1">  next</span><span style="color:#24292E">();</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">});</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// Route that will only be hit after the /admin middleware runs</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">app.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">get</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'/admin/dashboard'</span><span style="color:#24292E">, (</span><span style="color:#E36209">req</span><span style="color:#24292E">, </span><span style="color:#E36209">res</span><span style="color:#24292E">) </span><span style="color:#D73A49">=&gt;</span><span style="color:#24292E"> {</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#D73A49">  if</span><span style="color:#24292E"> (req.isAdmin) {</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">    res.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">send</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'Welcome to the Admin Dashboard!'</span><span style="color:#24292E">);</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">  } </span><span style="color:#D73A49">else</span><span style="color:#24292E"> {</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">    res.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">status</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#005CC5">403</span><span style="color:#24292E">).</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">send</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'Forbidden'</span><span style="color:#24292E">);</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">  }</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">});</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// ... (app.listen)</span></span></code></pre></div></div></div>
<ul>
<li>Any request to the server will trigger the global logging middleware, printing the request details to the console.</li>
<li>A request to <code>http://localhost:3000/admin/dashboard</code> will first trigger the global logger, then the <code>/admin</code> specific middleware (logging "Accessing admin section..."), and finally the <code>/admin/dashboard</code> route handler.</li>
</ul>
<h3>Built-in Middleware</h3>
<p>Express comes with built-in middleware functions. Two of the most common are <code>express.json()</code> and <code>express.urlencoded()</code>, used for parsing request bodies.</p>
<ul>
<li><code>express.json()</code>: Parses incoming requests with JSON payloads. It populates <code>req.body</code> with the parsed JSON data.</li>
<li><code>express.urlencoded({ extended: true })</code>: Parses incoming requests with URL-encoded payloads (typically from HTML forms). It also populates <code>req.body</code>. The <code>extended: true</code> option allows for rich objects and arrays to be encoded into the URL-encoded format.</li>
</ul>
<div class="not-prose my-6 max-w-full overflow-hidden rounded-lg border border-gray-200 has-[code:empty]:hidden"><div class="flex items-center justify-between gap-2 border-b border-gray-200 bg-gray-50 px-3 py-2"><span class="text-sm text-gray-600">javascript</span><div class="flex items-center gap-2"><button class="flex size-6 items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-md text-gray-400 hover:bg-zinc-200 hover:text-black focus:outline-none"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy size-3.5" aria-hidden="true"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"></rect><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"></path></svg></button></div></div><div class="mt-0 text-sm [&amp;_pre]:py-0 [&amp;_pre]:grid [&amp;_code]:py-4 [&amp;_code]:w-full [&amp;_code]:grid [&amp;_code]:overflow-x-auto [&amp;_code]:no-scrollbar [&amp;_code]:bg-transparent [&amp;_.line]:px-3 [&amp;_.line]:w-full [&amp;_.line]:relative [&amp;_.line]:min-h-5"><div><pre class="shiki github-light" style="background-color:#fff;color:#24292e" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// app.js (continuation)</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// ... (previous setup and routes)</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// Enable JSON body parsing for all incoming requests</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">app.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">use</span><span style="color:#24292E">(express.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">json</span><span style="color:#24292E">());</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// Enable URL-encoded body parsing for all incoming requests</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">app.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">use</span><span style="color:#24292E">(express.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">urlencoded</span><span style="color:#24292E">({ extended: </span><span style="color:#005CC5">true</span><span style="color:#24292E"> }));</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// POST route to handle user registration</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">app.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">post</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'/register'</span><span style="color:#24292E">, (</span><span style="color:#E36209">req</span><span style="color:#24292E">, </span><span style="color:#E36209">res</span><span style="color:#24292E">) </span><span style="color:#D73A49">=&gt;</span><span style="color:#24292E"> {</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">  // req.body will contain the parsed JSON or URL-encoded data</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#D73A49">  const</span><span style="color:#24292E"> { </span><span style="color:#005CC5">username</span><span style="color:#24292E">, </span><span style="color:#005CC5">email</span><span style="color:#24292E">, </span><span style="color:#005CC5">password</span><span style="color:#24292E"> } </span><span style="color:#D73A49">=</span><span style="color:#24292E"> req.body;</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#D73A49">  if</span><span style="color:#24292E"> (</span><span style="color:#D73A49">!</span><span style="color:#24292E">username </span><span style="color:#D73A49">||</span><span style="color:#D73A49"> !</span><span style="color:#24292E">email </span><span style="color:#D73A49">||</span><span style="color:#D73A49"> !</span><span style="color:#24292E">password) {</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#D73A49">    return</span><span style="color:#24292E"> res.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">status</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#005CC5">400</span><span style="color:#24292E">).</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">json</span><span style="color:#24292E">({ message: </span><span style="color:#032F62">'All fields are required'</span><span style="color:#24292E"> });</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">  }</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">  // In a real application, you would save this data to a database</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">  console.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">log</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'New user registered:'</span><span style="color:#24292E">, { username, email });</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">  res.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">status</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#005CC5">201</span><span style="color:#24292E">).</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">json</span><span style="color:#24292E">({ message: </span><span style="color:#032F62">'User registered successfully'</span><span style="color:#24292E">, user: { username, email } });</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">});</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// ... (app.listen)</span></span></code></pre></div></div></div>
<p>To test the <code>/register</code> route, you would typically use a tool like Postman or <code>curl</code>.</p>
<p><strong>Example using <code>curl</code> for JSON:</strong></p>
<div class="not-prose my-6 max-w-full overflow-hidden rounded-lg border border-gray-200 has-[code:empty]:hidden"><div class="flex items-center justify-between gap-2 border-b border-gray-200 bg-gray-50 px-3 py-2"><span class="text-sm text-gray-600">bash</span><div class="flex items-center gap-2"><button class="flex size-6 items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-md text-gray-400 hover:bg-zinc-200 hover:text-black focus:outline-none"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy size-3.5" aria-hidden="true"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"></rect><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"></path></svg></button></div></div><div class="mt-0 text-sm [&amp;_pre]:py-0 [&amp;_pre]:grid [&amp;_code]:py-4 [&amp;_code]:w-full [&amp;_code]:grid [&amp;_code]:overflow-x-auto [&amp;_code]:no-scrollbar [&amp;_code]:bg-transparent [&amp;_.line]:px-3 [&amp;_.line]:w-full [&amp;_.line]:relative [&amp;_.line]:min-h-5"><div><pre class="shiki github-light" style="background-color:#fff;color:#24292e" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#6F42C1">curl</span><span style="color:#005CC5"> -X</span><span style="color:#032F62"> POST</span><span style="color:#005CC5"> -H</span><span style="color:#032F62"> "Content-Type: application/json"</span><span style="color:#005CC5"> -d</span><span style="color:#032F62"> '{"username": "testuser", "email": "test@example.com", "password": "password123"}'</span><span style="color:#032F62"> http://localhost:3000/register</span></span></code></pre></div></div></div>
<p>The server will log "New user registered: { username: 'testuser', email: '<a href="mailto:test@example.com">test@example.com</a>' }" and respond with <code>{"message":"User registered successfully","user":{"username":"testuser","email":"test@example.com"}}</code>.</p>
<p><strong>Example using <code>curl</code> for URL-encoded (simulating a form submission):</strong></p>
<div class="not-prose my-6 max-w-full overflow-hidden rounded-lg border border-gray-200 has-[code:empty]:hidden"><div class="flex items-center justify-between gap-2 border-b border-gray-200 bg-gray-50 px-3 py-2"><span class="text-sm text-gray-600">bash</span><div class="flex items-center gap-2"><button class="flex size-6 items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-md text-gray-400 hover:bg-zinc-200 hover:text-black focus:outline-none"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy size-3.5" aria-hidden="true"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"></rect><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"></path></svg></button></div></div><div class="mt-0 text-sm [&amp;_pre]:py-0 [&amp;_pre]:grid [&amp;_code]:py-4 [&amp;_code]:w-full [&amp;_code]:grid [&amp;_code]:overflow-x-auto [&amp;_code]:no-scrollbar [&amp;_code]:bg-transparent [&amp;_.line]:px-3 [&amp;_.line]:w-full [&amp;_.line]:relative [&amp;_.line]:min-h-5"><div><pre class="shiki github-light" style="background-color:#fff;color:#24292e" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#6F42C1">curl</span><span style="color:#005CC5"> -X</span><span style="color:#032F62"> POST</span><span style="color:#005CC5"> -H</span><span style="color:#032F62"> "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded"</span><span style="color:#005CC5"> -d</span><span style="color:#032F62"> "username=anotheruser&amp;email=another@example.com&amp;password=securepassword"</span><span style="color:#032F62"> http://localhost:3000/register</span></span></code></pre></div></div></div>
<p>The server will log "New user registered: { username: 'anotheruser', email: '<a href="mailto:another@example.com">another@example.com</a>' }" and respond with the same JSON structure.</p>
<h3>Third-party Middleware</h3>
<p>Third-party middleware is typically installed via npm and used in the application to add specific functionalities. A common example is <code>cors</code> for enabling Cross-Origin Resource Sharing.</p>
<p>First, install the <code>cors</code> package:</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6 max-w-full overflow-hidden rounded-lg border border-gray-200 has-[code:empty]:hidden"><div class="flex items-center justify-between gap-2 border-b border-gray-200 bg-gray-50 px-3 py-2"><span class="text-sm text-gray-600">bash</span><div class="flex items-center gap-2"><button class="flex size-6 items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-md text-gray-400 hover:bg-zinc-200 hover:text-black focus:outline-none"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy size-3.5" aria-hidden="true"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"></rect><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"></path></svg></button></div></div><div class="mt-0 text-sm [&amp;_pre]:py-0 [&amp;_pre]:grid [&amp;_code]:py-4 [&amp;_code]:w-full [&amp;_code]:grid [&amp;_code]:overflow-x-auto [&amp;_code]:no-scrollbar [&amp;_code]:bg-transparent [&amp;_.line]:px-3 [&amp;_.line]:w-full [&amp;_.line]:relative [&amp;_.line]:min-h-5"><div><pre class="shiki github-light" style="background-color:#fff;color:#24292e" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#6F42C1">npm</span><span style="color:#032F62"> install</span><span style="color:#032F62"> cors</span></span></code></pre></div></div></div>
<p>Then, integrate it into your Express application:</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6 max-w-full overflow-hidden rounded-lg border border-gray-200 has-[code:empty]:hidden"><div class="flex items-center justify-between gap-2 border-b border-gray-200 bg-gray-50 px-3 py-2"><span class="text-sm text-gray-600">javascript</span><div class="flex items-center gap-2"><button class="flex size-6 items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-md text-gray-400 hover:bg-zinc-200 hover:text-black focus:outline-none"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy size-3.5" aria-hidden="true"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"></rect><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"></path></svg></button></div></div><div class="mt-0 text-sm [&amp;_pre]:py-0 [&amp;_pre]:grid [&amp;_code]:py-4 [&amp;_code]:w-full [&amp;_code]:grid [&amp;_code]:overflow-x-auto [&amp;_code]:no-scrollbar [&amp;_code]:bg-transparent [&amp;_.line]:px-3 [&amp;_.line]:w-full [&amp;_.line]:relative [&amp;_.line]:min-h-5"><div><pre class="shiki github-light" style="background-color:#fff;color:#24292e" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// app.js (continuation)</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// ... (previous setup and built-in middleware)</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#D73A49">const</span><span style="color:#005CC5"> cors</span><span style="color:#D73A49"> =</span><span style="color:#6F42C1"> require</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'cors'</span><span style="color:#24292E">); </span><span style="color:#6A737D">// Import the cors middleware</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// Enable CORS for all routes and origins</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">app.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">use</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">cors</span><span style="color:#24292E">());</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// You can also configure CORS for specific origins or methods</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">/*</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">app.use(cors({</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">  origin: 'http://example.com', // Allow only this origin</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">  methods: ['GET', 'POST']      // Allow only GET and POST requests</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">}));</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">*/</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">app.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">get</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'/api/resource'</span><span style="color:#24292E">, (</span><span style="color:#E36209">req</span><span style="color:#24292E">, </span><span style="color:#E36209">res</span><span style="color:#24292E">) </span><span style="color:#D73A49">=&gt;</span><span style="color:#24292E"> {</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">  res.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">json</span><span style="color:#24292E">({ message: </span><span style="color:#032F62">'This resource is accessible from any origin due to CORS.'</span><span style="color:#24292E"> });</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">});</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// ... (app.listen)</span></span></code></pre></div></div></div>
<p>With <code>cors()</code> enabled, a browser application hosted on a different domain (e.g., <code>http://my-frontend.com</code>) can make requests to <code>http://localhost:3000/api/resource</code> without encountering Cross-Origin errors. Without <code>cors</code>, the browser's security policy would block such requests.</p>
<h2>Exercises</h2>
<ol>
<li>
<p><strong>Basic Routing with Different Methods:</strong>
Modify the <code>app.js</code> file to include the following:</p>
<ul>
<li>A <code>GET</code> route <code>/data</code> that sends back a JSON object like <code>{ "id": 1, "name": "Sample Item" }</code>.</li>
<li>A <code>POST</code> route <code>/items</code> that expects a JSON body with <code>name</code> and <code>description</code> properties, logs them to the console, and sends back a 201 status with a success message in JSON.</li>
<li>A <code>PUT</code> route <code>/items/:id</code> that logs the <code>id</code> from parameters and a dummy <code>updatedData</code> from <code>req.body</code> (assume <code>express.json()</code> is in place), then responds with a success message including the <code>id</code>.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Route Parameters and Query Strings:</strong>
Create a <code>GET</code> route <code>/search</code> that expects two query parameters: <code>keyword</code> and <code>limit</code>.</p>
<ul>
<li>If <code>keyword</code> is provided, respond with a message like <code>Searching for: [keyword]</code>.</li>
<li>If <code>limit</code> is also provided, include <code>with a limit of: [limit]</code> in the message.</li>
<li>If neither is provided, respond with <code>Please provide a keyword for search.</code>.
<em>Hint: Query parameters are accessed via <code>req.query</code>.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Middleware for Request Timing:</strong>
Implement a new application-level middleware function that calculates the time taken for each request to be processed.</p>
<ul>
<li>The middleware should record the start time when a request comes in.</li>
<li>It should then define a <code>res.on('finish', ...)</code> event listener that calculates the difference between the start time and the finish time, and logs it to the console (e.g., <code>Request to / completed in 15ms</code>).</li>
<li>Apply this middleware globally using <code>app.use()</code>.</li>
<li>Test by accessing any route defined previously.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ol>
  
</div>

<div id="chapter-6.4">

<h1 class="mb-6 text-3xl font-semibold text-balance max-lg:mb-3 max-lg:text-xl">Handling HTTP Requests and Responses</h1><p>Node.js applications, particularly those built with Express.js, serve as the backend for web applications. The primary function of a backend is to receive requests from clients (like web browsers or mobile apps), process those requests, and send back appropriate responses. This interaction forms the core of how dynamic websites and applications function. Understanding how to handle these HTTP requests and craft meaningful HTTP responses is fundamental to building any server-side application.</p>
<h2>Understanding HTTP Requests</h2>
<p>HTTP requests are messages sent by the client to initiate an action on the server. An HTTP request consists of several parts: a method, a URL (Uniform Resource Locator), headers, and an optional body.</p>
<h3>HTTP Methods (Verbs)</h3>
<p>HTTP methods indicate the desired action to be performed for a given resource. Common methods include:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>GET:</strong> Used to request data from a specified resource. GET requests should only retrieve data and should have no other effect on the data. For example, retrieving a list of products from an e-commerce API.</li>
<li><strong>POST:</strong> Used to send data to a server to create a resource. The data sent to the server is included in the request body. For example, submitting a new user registration form or adding a new product to a catalog.</li>
<li><strong>PUT:</strong> Used to send data to a server to update or replace a resource with the request payload. If the resource does not exist, PUT can create it. For example, updating all fields of a user's profile.</li>
<li><strong>PATCH:</strong> Used to apply partial modifications to a resource. This is often used to update specific fields of an existing resource without sending the entire resource. For example, updating only a user's email address.</li>
<li><strong>DELETE:</strong> Used to delete the specified resource. For example, removing a specific product from the database.</li>
</ul>
<p>Consider a blog application.</p>
<ul>
<li>A <strong>GET</strong> request to <code>/posts</code> retrieves all blog posts.</li>
<li>A <strong>POST</strong> request to <code>/posts</code> with a new post's data in the body creates a new blog post.</li>
<li>A <strong>PUT</strong> request to <code>/posts/123</code> with updated data replaces the entire blog post with ID <code>123</code>.</li>
<li>A <strong>PATCH</strong> request to <code>/posts/123</code> with only a new <code>title</code> updates just the title of blog post <code>123</code>.</li>
<li>A <strong>DELETE</strong> request to <code>/posts/123</code> removes the blog post with ID <code>123</code>.</li>
</ul>
<h3>Request URL and Parameters</h3>
<p>The URL identifies the resource on the server that the request targets. URLs can include query parameters or route parameters to provide additional information to the server.</p>
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>Query Parameters:</strong> These are appended to the URL after a <code>?</code> and are typically used for filtering, sorting, or pagination. Multiple parameters are separated by <code>&amp;</code>.</p>
<ul>
<li>Example: <code>/products?category=electronics&amp;sort=price</code></li>
<li>In an Express application, query parameters are accessible via <code>req.query</code>. If the URL is <code>/products?category=electronics</code>, then <code>req.query.category</code> would be <code>'electronics'</code>.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Route Parameters:</strong> These are parts of the URL path that represent variable segments. They are often used to identify a specific resource.</p>
<ul>
<li>Example: <code>/users/123</code> where <code>123</code> is the user ID.</li>
<li>In an Express route defined as <code>/users/:id</code>, the route parameter <code>id</code> is accessible via <code>req.params.id</code>. So, <code>req.params.id</code> would be <code>'123'</code>.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h3>Request Headers</h3>
<p>Headers provide metadata about the request and the client. They convey information such as the client's preferred language, the type of content it expects, or authentication credentials.</p>
<ul>
<li><code>Content-Type</code>: Specifies the media type of the request body (e.g., <code>application/json</code>, <code>application/x-www-form-urlencoded</code>).</li>
<li><code>Accept</code>: Indicates the media types the client can process (e.g., <code>application/json</code>).</li>
<li><code>Authorization</code>: Contains authentication credentials (e.g., a JWT token).</li>
</ul>
<p>In Express, request headers are accessible via <code>req.headers</code>. For example, <code>req.headers['content-type']</code>.</p>
<h3>Request Body</h3>
<p>The request body contains the data sent by the client to the server, typically with <code>POST</code>, <code>PUT</code>, or <code>PATCH</code> requests. The format of the body is specified by the <code>Content-Type</code> header. Common formats include JSON or URL-encoded form data.</p>
<ul>
<li>When submitting a form, the body might contain key-value pairs representing form fields.</li>
<li>When sending data to a REST API, the body is often a JSON object.</li>
</ul>
<p>In Express, the request body is accessible via <code>req.body</code>, but it requires middleware (like <code>express.json()</code> or <code>express.urlencoded()</code>) to parse it into a usable JavaScript object.</p>
<h2>Crafting HTTP Responses</h2>
<p>After processing a request, the server sends an HTTP response back to the client. An HTTP response also includes a status code, headers, and an optional body.</p>
<h3>HTTP Status Codes</h3>
<p>Status codes are three-digit numbers indicating the outcome of the request. They are grouped into five classes:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>1xx Informational:</strong> The request was received, continuing process. (Rarely used in typical web applications)</li>
<li><strong>2xx Success:</strong> The request was successfully received, understood, and accepted.
<ul>
<li><code>200 OK</code>: Standard response for successful HTTP requests.</li>
<li><code>201 Created</code>: The request has been fulfilled and resulted in a new resource being created.</li>
<li><code>204 No Content</code>: The server successfully processed the request, but is not returning any content.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>3xx Redirection:</strong> Further action needs to be taken by the user agent to fulfill the request.
<ul>
<li><code>301 Moved Permanently</code>: The resource has been permanently moved to a new URL.</li>
<li><code>302 Found</code>: The resource is temporarily located at a different URI.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>4xx Client Error:</strong> The request contains bad syntax or cannot be fulfilled.
<ul>
<li><code>400 Bad Request</code>: The server cannot or will not process the request due to an apparent client error (e.g., malformed request syntax, invalid request message framing, or deceptive request routing).</li>
<li><code>401 Unauthorized</code>: Authentication is required and has failed or has not yet been provided.</li>
<li><code>403 Forbidden</code>: The client does not have access rights to the content.</li>
<li><code>44 Not Found</code>: The server cannot find the requested resource.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>5xx Server Error:</strong> The server failed to fulfill an apparently valid request.
<ul>
<li><code>500 Internal Server Error</code>: A generic error message, given when an unexpected condition was encountered and no more specific message is suitable.</li>
<li><code>503 Service Unavailable</code>: The server is currently unable to handle the request due to a temporary overload or scheduled maintenance, which will likely be alleviated after some delay.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<p>Using the blog application example:</p>
<ul>
<li>After successfully creating a new post, the server might respond with <code>201 Created</code>.</li>
<li>If a user tries to access a post with an ID that doesn't exist, the server responds with <code>404 Not Found</code>.</li>
<li>If an error occurs on the server while trying to process a request, it might respond with <code>500 Internal Server Error</code>.</li>
</ul>
<h3>Response Headers</h3>
<p>Similar to request headers, response headers provide metadata about the response and the server.</p>
<ul>
<li><code>Content-Type</code>: Specifies the media type of the response body (e.g., <code>application/json</code>, <code>text/html</code>).</li>
<li><code>Cache-Control</code>: Directives for caching mechanisms in both requests and responses.</li>
<li><code>Location</code>: Used with <code>3xx</code> status codes to indicate the URI to which the client should redirect.</li>
</ul>
<p>In Express, you can set response headers using <code>res.setHeader()</code> or <code>res.set()</code>.</p>
<h3>Response Body</h3>
<p>The response body contains the data the server sends back to the client. This can be HTML, JSON, plain text, or any other type of data.</p>
<ul>
<li>For an API endpoint, the body is typically a JSON object or array.</li>
<li>For a web page, the body is typically HTML content.</li>
</ul>
<p>In Express, various methods are available for sending response bodies, such as <code>res.send()</code>, <code>res.json()</code>, <code>res.render()</code>, and <code>res.end()</code>.</p>
<h2>Practical Examples with Express.js</h2>
<p>Let's expand on the Express.js server we started building in the previous lesson ("Introduction to Express.js: Routing and Middleware"). We will demonstrate how to handle different types of requests and send appropriate responses.</p>
<p>First, ensure you have an <code>app.js</code> file (or similar) set up with Express:</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6 max-w-full overflow-hidden rounded-lg border border-gray-200 has-[code:empty]:hidden"><div class="flex items-center justify-between gap-2 border-b border-gray-200 bg-gray-50 px-3 py-2"><span class="text-sm text-gray-600">javascript</span><div class="flex items-center gap-2"><button class="flex size-6 items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-md text-gray-400 hover:bg-zinc-200 hover:text-black focus:outline-none"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy size-3.5" aria-hidden="true"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"></rect><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"></path></svg></button></div></div><div class="mt-0 text-sm [&amp;_pre]:py-0 [&amp;_pre]:grid [&amp;_code]:py-4 [&amp;_code]:w-full [&amp;_code]:grid [&amp;_code]:overflow-x-auto [&amp;_code]:no-scrollbar [&amp;_code]:bg-transparent [&amp;_.line]:px-3 [&amp;_.line]:w-full [&amp;_.line]:relative [&amp;_.line]:min-h-5"><div><pre class="shiki github-light" style="background-color:#fff;color:#24292e" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// app.js</span></span>

<span class="line"><span style="color:#D73A49">const</span><span style="color:#005CC5"> app</span><span style="color:#D73A49"> =</span><span style="color:#6F42C1"> express</span><span style="color:#24292E">();</span></span>

<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">});</span></span></code></pre></div></div></div>
<p>Now, let's add routes to handle different HTTP requests.</p>
<h3>GET Requests: Retrieving Resources</h3>
<div class="not-prose my-6 max-w-full overflow-hidden rounded-lg border border-gray-200 has-[code:empty]:hidden"><div class="flex items-center justify-between gap-2 border-b border-gray-200 bg-gray-50 px-3 py-2"><span class="text-sm text-gray-600">javascript</span><div class="flex items-center gap-2"><button class="flex size-6 items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-md text-gray-400 hover:bg-zinc-200 hover:text-black focus:outline-none"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy size-3.5" aria-hidden="true"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"></rect><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"></path></svg></button></div></div><div class="mt-0 text-sm [&amp;_pre]:py-0 [&amp;_pre]:grid [&amp;_code]:py-4 [&amp;_code]:w-full [&amp;_code]:grid [&amp;_code]:overflow-x-auto [&amp;_code]:no-scrollbar [&amp;_code]:bg-transparent [&amp;_.line]:px-3 [&amp;_.line]:w-full [&amp;_.line]:relative [&amp;_.line]:min-h-5"><div><pre class="shiki github-light" style="background-color:#fff;color:#24292e" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// app.js (continued)</span></span>
