What two essential HTML attributes/tags and corresponding CSS properties would you need to add to make it keyboard-operable and visibly focused?</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6 max-w-full overflow-hidden rounded-lg border border-gray-200 has-[code:empty]:hidden"><div class="flex items-center justify-between gap-2 border-b border-gray-200 bg-gray-50 px-3 py-2"><span class="text-sm text-gray-600">html</span><div class="flex items-center gap-2"><button class="flex size-6 items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-md text-gray-400 hover:bg-zinc-200 hover:text-black focus:outline-none"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy size-3.5" aria-hidden="true"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"></rect><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"></path></svg></button></div></div><div class="mt-0 text-sm [&amp;_pre]:py-0 [&amp;_pre]:grid [&amp;_code]:py-4 [&amp;_code]:w-full [&amp;_code]:grid [&amp;_code]:overflow-x-auto [&amp;_code]:no-scrollbar [&amp;_code]:bg-transparent [&amp;_.line]:px-3 [&amp;_.line]:w-full [&amp;_.line]:relative [&amp;_.line]:min-h-5"><div><pre class="shiki github-light" style="background-color:#fff;color:#24292e" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">&lt;</span><span style="color:#22863A">div</span><span style="color:#6F42C1"> class</span><span style="color:#24292E">=</span><span style="color:#032F62">"custom-button"</span><span style="color:#24292E">&gt;Click Me&lt;/</span><span style="color:#22863A">div</span><span style="color:#24292E">&gt;</span></span></code></pre></div></div></div>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Color Contrast:</strong> You have a website with a light blue background (<code>#ADD8E6</code>). You want to use a contrasting text color for better readability. Suggest two text colors (hex codes) that would pass WCAG AA contrast requirements. (Hint: A contrast checker tool might be helpful here.)</p>
</li>
</ol>
<h2>Real-World Application</h2>
<p>Accessibility is not just a compliance checkbox; it's about creating inclusive digital experiences.</p>
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>Example 1: Government Websites:</strong> Government websites (e.g., IRS.gov, NHS.uk) are legally mandated to be accessible. This ensures all citizens, regardless of ability, can access vital information and services like filing taxes, applying for benefits, or finding health resources. They rigorously implement WCAG standards, providing accessible forms, properly structured content, and keyboard-only navigation. For instance, the US Department of Justice website often uses a clear, high-contrast design and ensures all documents have accessible text alternatives.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Example 2: E-commerce Platforms:</strong> Major e-commerce sites (e.g., Amazon, Etsy) strive for accessibility to reach the widest possible customer base. An accessible shopping experience means visually impaired users can navigate product listings with screen readers (due to proper <code>alt</code> text and semantic headings), keyboard-only users can add items to carts and complete checkout, and users with cognitive disabilities can understand clear product descriptions and instructions. If Amazon's product images lacked <code>alt</code> text, millions of potential customers would be unable to shop effectively.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Hypothetical Scenario:</strong> Consider a new online learning platform that aims to serve students globally. If this platform neglects accessibility, a student with dyslexia might struggle with poorly formatted text, a student with a visual impairment wouldn't be able to engage with video lectures lacking audio descriptions, and a student with limited hand mobility might be unable to complete interactive quizzes that only rely on mouse input. By integrating accessibility from the start, the platform ensures all students have an equal opportunity to learn and succeed, leading to broader adoption and a more positive impact.</p>
</li>
</ul>
  
</div>

<div id="chapter-7.5">

<h1 class="mb-6 text-3xl font-semibold text-balance max-lg:mb-3 max-lg:text-xl">Deploying Your Application to Netlify or Heroku</h1><p>Deploying a full-stack application involves making both your front-end and back-end accessible on the internet. This process, often referred to as web hosting, allows users to interact with your application without running it locally. Services like Netlify and Heroku provide platforms to simplify this deployment, offering robust infrastructure and tools to manage your application's public availability.</p>
<h2>Understanding Deployment Platforms</h2>
<p>Deployment platforms automate much of the traditional server setup and maintenance, allowing developers to focus on building applications. These platforms typically integrate with version control systems like Git, enabling continuous deployment where changes pushed to a repository automatically trigger a new deployment.</p>
<h3>Netlify for Front-End Deployment</h3>
<p>Netlify is a popular platform primarily known for hosting static sites and front-end applications. It excels at deploying projects built with frameworks like React, which produce static assets (HTML, CSS, JavaScript files) that can be served directly to browsers.</p>
<p><strong>Key Features of Netlify:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Continuous Deployment:</strong> Connects directly to Git repositories (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket). Any push to a specified branch automatically triggers a build and deployment.</li>
<li><strong>Global CDN:</strong> Distributes your site's assets across servers worldwide, improving loading speeds for users regardless of their location.</li>
<li><strong>Custom Domains:</strong> Allows you to use your own domain name (e.g., <code>www.your-app.com</code>) instead of a Netlify subdomain.</li>
<li><strong>SSL Certificates:</strong> Automatically provides and renews free SSL certificates (HTTPS) for secure connections.</li>
<li><strong>Serverless Functions:</strong> Supports serverless functions (Netlify Functions) for back-end logic, which can be useful for simpler API needs, though our full Node.js/Express back-end will be handled separately.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Deployment Process with Netlify:</strong></p>
<ol>
<li><strong>Prepare your Front-End:</strong> Ensure your React application is production-ready. This usually involves running a build script, which compiles your React code into static files in a <code>build</code> or <code>dist</code> directory. For a React app created with Create React App, this is typically done using <code>npm run build</code> or <code>yarn build</code>.</li>
<li><strong>Connect to Git:</strong> Sign up for Netlify and connect your Git repository.</li>
<li><strong>Configure Build Settings:</strong>
<ul>
<li><strong>Repository:</strong> Select the repository containing your front-end code.</li>
<li><strong>Branch to deploy:</strong> Choose the branch (e.g., <code>main</code> or <code>master</code>) that Netlify should monitor for changes.</li>
<li><strong>Build command:</strong> Specify the command Netlify should run to build your project (e.g., <code>npm run build</code>).</li>
<li><strong>Publish directory:</strong> Indicate the folder where your compiled static files are located after the build command runs (e.g., <code>build</code>).</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Deploy:</strong> Netlify will automatically build and deploy your application. Subsequent pushes to the configured branch will trigger new deployments.</li>
</ol>
<p><strong>Example: Deploying a React Front-End to Netlify</strong></p>
<p>Imagine your React application is structured like this:</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6 max-w-full overflow-hidden rounded-lg border border-gray-200 has-[code:empty]:hidden"><div class="flex items-center justify-between gap-2 border-b border-gray-200 bg-gray-50 px-3 py-2"><span class="text-sm text-gray-600">javascript</span><div class="flex items-center gap-2"><button class="flex size-6 items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-md text-gray-400 hover:bg-zinc-200 hover:text-black focus:outline-none"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy size-3.5" aria-hidden="true"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"></rect><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"></path></svg></button></div></div><div class="mt-0 text-sm [&amp;_pre]:py-0 [&amp;_pre]:grid [&amp;_code]:py-4 [&amp;_code]:w-full [&amp;_code]:grid [&amp;_code]:overflow-x-auto [&amp;_code]:no-scrollbar [&amp;_code]:bg-transparent [&amp;_.line]:px-3 [&amp;_.line]:w-full [&amp;_.line]:relative [&amp;_.line]:min-h-5"><div><pre class="shiki github-light" style="background-color:#fff;color:#24292e" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">my</span><span style="color:#D73A49">-</span><span style="color:#24292E">fullstack</span><span style="color:#D73A49">-</span><span style="color:#24292E">app</span><span style="color:#D73A49">/</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">├── frontend</span><span style="color:#D73A49">/</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">│   ├── public</span><span style="color:#D73A49">/</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">│   ├── src</span><span style="color:#D73A49">/</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">│   ├── package.json</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">│   └── </span><span style="color:#D73A49">...</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">└── backend</span><span style="color:#D73A49">/</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">    ├── server.js</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">    ├── package.json</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">    └── </span><span style="color:#D73A49">...</span></span></code></pre></div></div></div>
<p>To deploy only the <code>frontend</code> part to Netlify, you would typically:</p>
<ol>
<li>Navigate to your <code>frontend</code> directory: <code>cd frontend</code></li>
<li>Run the build command: <code>npm run build</code> (This creates a <code>build</code> folder inside <code>frontend</code>).</li>
<li>In Netlify, when connecting your repository, you might need to specify the <strong>base directory</strong> as <code>frontend/</code> if your repository root is <code>my-fullstack-app/</code>.</li>
<li>Set the <strong>build command</strong> to <code>npm run build</code>.</li>
<li>Set the <strong>publish directory</strong> to <code>frontend/build</code> (or just <code>build</code> if your base directory is <code>frontend</code>).</li>
</ol>
<p>This configuration tells Netlify to go into the <code>frontend</code> directory, run the build script, and then serve the contents of the <code>build</code> folder found within that <code>frontend</code> directory.</p>
<h3>Heroku for Back-End Deployment</h3>
<p>Heroku is a platform-as-a-service (PaaS) that supports a wide range of programming languages and frameworks, including Node.js. It is well-suited for deploying our Express.js back-end application. Heroku provides a "dyno" (a lightweight Linux container) to run your application and manages the underlying infrastructure.</p>
<p><strong>Key Features of Heroku:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Language Support (Buildpacks):</strong> Heroku uses buildpacks to detect your application's language (e.g., Node.js) and provide the necessary runtime and dependencies.</li>
<li><strong>Dynos:</strong> Your application runs in isolated containers called dynos. You can scale dynos up or down based on your application's traffic.</li>
<li><strong>Add-ons:</strong> Provides a marketplace of add-ons for services like databases (e.g., PostgreSQL, MongoDB), caching, logging, etc. We would use an add-on for MongoDB or connect to an external MongoDB Atlas cluster.</li>
<li><strong>Git Integration:</strong> Deployments are often done directly from Git using the Heroku CLI.</li>
<li><strong>Environment Variables:</strong> Securely manage configuration variables (like database credentials, API keys) without hardcoding them into your application code.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Deployment Process with Heroku:</strong></p>
<ol>
<li><strong>Prepare your Back-End:</strong>
<ul>
<li><strong>Port Configuration:</strong> Heroku assigns a dynamic port to your application. Your Node.js/Express server must listen to the port specified by the <code>process.env.PORT</code> environment variable.
<div class="not-prose my-6 max-w-full overflow-hidden rounded-lg border border-gray-200 has-[code:empty]:hidden"><div class="flex items-center justify-between gap-2 border-b border-gray-200 bg-gray-50 px-3 py-2"><span class="text-sm text-gray-600">javascript</span><div class="flex items-center gap-2"><button class="flex size-6 items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-md text-gray-400 hover:bg-zinc-200 hover:text-black focus:outline-none"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy size-3.5" aria-hidden="true"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"></rect><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"></path></svg></button></div></div><div class="mt-0 text-sm [&amp;_pre]:py-0 [&amp;_pre]:grid [&amp;_code]:py-4 [&amp;_code]:w-full [&amp;_code]:grid [&amp;_code]:overflow-x-auto [&amp;_code]:no-scrollbar [&amp;_code]:bg-transparent [&amp;_.line]:px-3 [&amp;_.line]:w-full [&amp;_.line]:relative [&amp;_.line]:min-h-5"><div><pre class="shiki github-light" style="background-color:#fff;color:#24292e" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// server.js</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#D73A49">const</span><span style="color:#005CC5"> app</span><span style="color:#D73A49"> =</span><span style="color:#6F42C1"> require</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'./app'</span><span style="color:#24292E">); </span><span style="color:#6A737D">// Assuming your Express app logic is in app.js</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#D73A49">const</span><span style="color:#005CC5"> PORT</span><span style="color:#D73A49"> =</span><span style="color:#24292E"> process.env.</span><span style="color:#005CC5">PORT</span><span style="color:#D73A49"> ||</span><span style="color:#005CC5"> 5000</span><span style="color:#24292E">; </span><span style="color:#6A737D">// Use Heroku's port or default to 5000 locally</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">app.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">listen</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#005CC5">PORT</span><span style="color:#24292E">, () </span><span style="color:#D73A49">=&gt;</span><span style="color:#24292E"> {</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">    console.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">log</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">`Server running on port ${</span><span style="color:#005CC5">PORT</span><span style="color:#032F62">}`</span><span style="color:#24292E">);</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">});</span></span></code></pre></div></div></div>
</li>
<li><strong>Procfile:</strong> Create a file named <code>Procfile</code> (no extension) in the root of your back-end project. This file tells Heroku how to start your application.
<div class="not-prose my-6 max-w-full overflow-hidden rounded-lg border border-gray-200 has-[code:empty]:hidden"><div class="flex items-center justify-between gap-2 border-b border-gray-200 bg-gray-50 px-3 py-2"><span class="text-sm text-gray-600">javascript</span><div class="flex items-center gap-2"><button class="flex size-6 items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-md text-gray-400 hover:bg-zinc-200 hover:text-black focus:outline-none"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy size-3.5" aria-hidden="true"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"></rect><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"></path></svg></button></div></div><div class="mt-0 text-sm [&amp;_pre]:py-0 [&amp;_pre]:grid [&amp;_code]:py-4 [&amp;_code]:w-full [&amp;_code]:grid [&amp;_code]:overflow-x-auto [&amp;_code]:no-scrollbar [&amp;_code]:bg-transparent [&amp;_.line]:px-3 [&amp;_.line]:w-full [&amp;_.line]:relative [&amp;_.line]:min-h-5"><div><pre class="shiki github-light" style="background-color:#fff;color:#24292e" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#6F42C1">web</span><span style="color:#24292E">: node server.js</span></span></code></pre></div></div></div>
If your main server file is named <code>index.js</code>, it would be <code>web: node index.js</code>.</li>
<li><strong>Dependencies:</strong> Ensure all your dependencies are listed in <code>package.json</code> and installable via <code>npm install</code> or <code>yarn install</code>. Heroku uses <code>package.json</code> to install dependencies.</li>
<li><strong>Scripts:</strong> Make sure you have a <code>start</code> script in your <code>package.json</code> (though Heroku's buildpack often defaults to <code>node server.js</code> for Node apps if a Procfile is present).
<div class="not-prose my-6 max-w-full overflow-hidden rounded-lg border border-gray-200 has-[code:empty]:hidden"><div class="flex items-center justify-between gap-2 border-b border-gray-200 bg-gray-50 px-3 py-2"><span class="text-sm text-gray-600">json</span><div class="flex items-center gap-2"><button class="flex size-6 items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-md text-gray-400 hover:bg-zinc-200 hover:text-black focus:outline-none"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy size-3.5" aria-hidden="true"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"></rect><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"></path></svg></button></div></div><div class="mt-0 text-sm [&amp;_pre]:py-0 [&amp;_pre]:grid [&amp;_code]:py-4 [&amp;_code]:w-full [&amp;_code]:grid [&amp;_code]:overflow-x-auto [&amp;_code]:no-scrollbar [&amp;_code]:bg-transparent [&amp;_.line]:px-3 [&amp;_.line]:w-full [&amp;_.line]:relative [&amp;_.line]:min-h-5"><div><pre class="shiki github-light" style="background-color:#fff;color:#24292e" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// package.json in your backend directory</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">{</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#005CC5">  "name"</span><span style="color:#24292E">: </span><span style="color:#032F62">"my-backend"</span><span style="color:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#005CC5">  "version"</span><span style="color:#24292E">: </span><span style="color:#032F62">"1.0.0"</span><span style="color:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#005CC5">  "description"</span><span style="color:#24292E">: </span><span style="color:#032F62">""</span><span style="color:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#005CC5">  "main"</span><span style="color:#24292E">: </span><span style="color:#032F62">"server.js"</span><span style="color:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#005CC5">  "scripts"</span><span style="color:#24292E">: {</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#005CC5">    "start"</span><span style="color:#24292E">: </span><span style="color:#032F62">"node server.js"</span><span style="color:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#005CC5">    "dev"</span><span style="color:#24292E">: </span><span style="color:#032F62">"nodemon server.js"</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">  },</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#005CC5">  "keywords"</span><span style="color:#24292E">: [],</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#005CC5">  "author"</span><span style="color:#24292E">: </span><span style="color:#032F62">""</span><span style="color:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#005CC5">  "license"</span><span style="color:#24292E">: </span><span style="color:#032F62">"ISC"</span><span style="color:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#005CC5">  "dependencies"</span><span style="color:#24292E">: {</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#005CC5">    "express"</span><span style="color:#24292E">: </span><span style="color:#032F62">"^4.17.1"</span><span style="color:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#005CC5">    "mongoose"</span><span style="color:#24292E">: </span><span style="color:#032F62">"^6.0.0"</span><span style="color:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">    // ... other dependencies</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">  }</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">}</span></span></code></pre></div></div></div>
</li>
<li><strong>Database Connection:</strong> Configure your application to connect to your MongoDB database using environment variables for sensitive credentials. We explored connecting to MongoDB in Module 6. For Heroku, you'd typically use a MongoDB Atlas connection string.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Install Heroku CLI:</strong> Download and install the Heroku Command Line Interface.</li>
<li><strong>Log in to Heroku CLI:</strong> <code>heroku login</code></li>
<li><strong>Create a Heroku App:</strong> From your back-end project directory: <code>heroku create your-app-name</code> (replace <code>your-app-name</code> with a unique name). This creates a new Heroku application and sets up a Git remote.</li>
<li><strong>Set Environment Variables:</strong> Configure your database connection string and any other sensitive variables.
<div class="not-prose my-6 max-w-full overflow-hidden rounded-lg border border-gray-200 has-[code:empty]:hidden"><div class="flex items-center justify-between gap-2 border-b border-gray-200 bg-gray-50 px-3 py-2"><span class="text-sm text-gray-600">bash</span><div class="flex items-center gap-2"><button class="flex size-6 items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-md text-gray-400 hover:bg-zinc-200 hover:text-black focus:outline-none"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy size-3.5" aria-hidden="true"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"></rect><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"></path></svg></button></div></div><div class="mt-0 text-sm [&amp;_pre]:py-0 [&amp;_pre]:grid [&amp;_code]:py-4 [&amp;_code]:w-full [&amp;_code]:grid [&amp;_code]:overflow-x-auto [&amp;_code]:no-scrollbar [&amp;_code]:bg-transparent [&amp;_.line]:px-3 [&amp;_.line]:w-full [&amp;_.line]:relative [&amp;_.line]:min-h-5"><div><pre class="shiki github-light" style="background-color:#fff;color:#24292e" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#6F42C1">heroku</span><span style="color:#032F62"> config:set</span><span style="color:#032F62"> MONGODB_URI="your_mongodb_atlas_connection_string"</span><span style="color:#032F62"> JWT_SECRET="your_secret_key"</span></span></code></pre></div></div></div>
</li>
<li><strong>Deploy from Git:</strong> Push your back-end code to the Heroku Git remote.
<div class="not-prose my-6 max-w-full overflow-hidden rounded-lg border border-gray-200 has-[code:empty]:hidden"><div class="flex items-center justify-between gap-2 border-b border-gray-200 bg-gray-50 px-3 py-2"><span class="text-sm text-gray-600">bash</span><div class="flex items-center gap-2"><button class="flex size-6 items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-md text-gray-400 hover:bg-zinc-200 hover:text-black focus:outline-none"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy size-3.5" aria-hidden="true"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"></rect><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"></path></svg></button></div></div><div class="mt-0 text-sm [&amp;_pre]:py-0 [&amp;_pre]:grid [&amp;_code]:py-4 [&amp;_code]:w-full [&amp;_code]:grid [&amp;_code]:overflow-x-auto [&amp;_code]:no-scrollbar [&amp;_code]:bg-transparent [&amp;_.line]:px-3 [&amp;_.line]:w-full [&amp;_.line]:relative [&amp;_.line]:min-h-5"><div><pre class="shiki github-light" style="background-color:#fff;color:#24292e" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#6F42C1">git</span><span style="color:#032F62"> add</span><span style="color:#032F62"> .</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6F42C1">git</span><span style="color:#032F62"> commit</span><span style="color:#005CC5"> -m</span><span style="color:#032F62"> "Initial Heroku deployment"</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6F42C1">git</span><span style="color:#032F62"> push</span><span style="color:#032F62"> heroku</span><span style="color:#032F62"> main</span><span style="color:#6A737D"> # Or master, depending on your branch name</span></span></code></pre></div></div></div>
Heroku will detect your Node.js application, install dependencies, and start your server based on the <code>Procfile</code>.</li>
<li><strong>Open the App:</strong> <code>heroku open</code> to view your deployed back-end's root URL.</li>
</ol>
<p><strong>Example: Deploying a Node.js/Express Back-End to Heroku</strong></p>
<p>Assuming your <code>backend</code> directory contains your Express application and <code>server.js</code> is the entry point:</p>
<ol>
<li>Make sure <code>server.js</code> uses <code>process.env.PORT</code>.</li>
<li>Create a <code>Procfile</code> in the <code>backend</code> directory with <code>web: node server.js</code>.</li>
<li>From the <code>backend</code> directory, initialize a Git repository if you haven't already: <code>git init</code>.</li>
<li>Create a Heroku app: <code>heroku create my-express-api</code>.</li>
<li>Set your MongoDB URI: <code>heroku config:set MONGODB_URI="mongodb+srv://user:pass@cluster.mongodb.net/mydb?retryWrites=true&amp;w=majority"</code>.</li>
<li>Commit your changes: <code>git add . &amp;&amp; git commit -m "Prepare for Heroku deployment"</code>.</li>
<li>Push to Heroku: <code>git push heroku main</code>.</li>
</ol>
<p>Heroku will then build and deploy your API, making it accessible at <code>https://my-express-api.herokuapp.com/</code>. Your front-end application (deployed on Netlify) will then need to make API calls to this Heroku URL.</p>
<h2>Connecting Front-End and Back-End</h2>
<p>Once both your front-end and back-end are deployed, the front-end application needs to know where to send its API requests. This means changing the API endpoint in your React application from a local development URL (e.g., <code>http://localhost:5000</code>) to your deployed Heroku back-end URL (e.g., <code>https://my-express-api.herokuapp.com</code>).</p>
<p><strong>Steps to Connect:</strong></p>
<ol>
<li>
<p><strong>Identify Back-End URL:</strong> After deploying your back-end to Heroku, note down its URL (e.g., <code>https://your-heroku-app-name.herokuapp.com</code>).</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Update Front-End API Calls:</strong> In your React front-end code, wherever you are making <code>fetch</code> or <code>axios</code> requests to your back-end, update the base URL.</p>
<p><strong>Example:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Before (development):</strong>
<div class="not-prose my-6 max-w-full overflow-hidden rounded-lg border border-gray-200 has-[code:empty]:hidden"><div class="flex items-center justify-between gap-2 border-b border-gray-200 bg-gray-50 px-3 py-2"><span class="text-sm text-gray-600">javascript</span><div class="flex items-center gap-2"><button class="flex size-6 items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-md text-gray-400 hover:bg-zinc-200 hover:text-black focus:outline-none"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy size-3.5" aria-hidden="true"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"></rect><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"></path></svg></button></div></div><div class="mt-0 text-sm [&amp;_pre]:py-0 [&amp;_pre]:grid [&amp;_code]:py-4 [&amp;_code]:w-full [&amp;_code]:grid [&amp;_code]:overflow-x-auto [&amp;_code]:no-scrollbar [&amp;_code]:bg-transparent [&amp;_.line]:px-3 [&amp;_.line]:w-full [&amp;_.line]:relative [&amp;_.line]:min-h-5"><div><pre class="shiki github-light" style="background-color:#fff;color:#24292e" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#6F42C1">fetch</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'http://localhost:5000/api/items'</span><span style="color:#24292E">)</span></span></code></pre></div></div></div>
</li>
<li><strong>After (production):</strong>
<div class="not-prose my-6 max-w-full overflow-hidden rounded-lg border border-gray-200 has-[code:empty]:hidden"><div class="flex items-center justify-between gap-2 border-b border-gray-200 bg-gray-50 px-3 py-2"><span class="text-sm text-gray-600">javascript</span><div class="flex items-center gap-2"><button class="flex size-6 items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-md text-gray-400 hover:bg-zinc-200 hover:text-black focus:outline-none"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy size-3.5" aria-hidden="true"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"></rect><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"></path></svg></button></div></div><div class="mt-0 text-sm [&amp;_pre]:py-0 [&amp;_pre]:grid [&amp;_code]:py-4 [&amp;_code]:w-full [&amp;_code]:grid [&amp;_code]:overflow-x-auto [&amp;_code]:no-scrollbar [&amp;_code]:bg-transparent [&amp;_.line]:px-3 [&amp;_.line]:w-full [&amp;_.line]:relative [&amp;_.line]:min-h-5"><div><pre class="shiki github-light" style="background-color:#fff;color:#24292e" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// You might use an environment variable for the API URL</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#D73A49">const</span><span style="color:#005CC5"> API_BASE_URL</span><span style="color:#D73A49"> =</span><span style="color:#24292E"> process.env.</span><span style="color:#005CC5">REACT_APP_API_URL</span><span style="color:#D73A49"> ||</span><span style="color:#032F62"> 'http://localhost:5000'</span><span style="color:#24292E">;</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6F42C1">fetch</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">`${</span><span style="color:#005CC5">API_BASE_URL</span><span style="color:#032F62">}/api/items`</span><span style="color:#24292E">)</span></span></code></pre></div></div></div>
</li>
</ul>
<p>When deploying to Netlify, you would set <code>REACT_APP_API_URL</code> as an environment variable in Netlify's build settings to your Heroku app's URL. This approach is superior to hardcoding the URL, allowing you to easily switch between development and production environments.</p>
<p><strong>Configuring Environment Variables in Netlify:</strong></p>
<ol>
<li>Go to your Netlify site settings.</li>
<li>Navigate to "Build &amp; deploy" &gt; "Environment".</li>
<li>Add new environment variables, for example: <code>REACT_APP_API_URL</code> with the value <code>https://your-heroku-app-name.herokuapp.com</code>.</li>
<li>Trigger a new deploy for these changes to take effect.</li>
</ol>
</li>
</ol>
<h2>Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS)</h2>
<p>When your front-end (e.g., <code>your-netlify-app.netlify.app</code>) makes requests to your back-end (e.g., <code>your-heroku-app.herokuapp.com</code>), these are <em>cross-origin</em> requests because they originate from different domains. By default, web browsers block cross-origin requests for security reasons. This is where CORS comes in.</p>
<p>To allow your front-end to communicate with your back-end, you need to configure your Express.js back-end to allow requests from your Netlify front-end domain. This is typically done using the <code>cors</code> npm package.</p>
<p><strong>Example: Configuring CORS in Express.js (Module 6 Refresher)</strong></p>
<p>In your <code>backend/server.js</code> or <code>backend/app.js</code> file:</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6 max-w-full overflow-hidden rounded-lg border border-gray-200 has-[code:empty]:hidden"><div class="flex items-center justify-between gap-2 border-b border-gray-200 bg-gray-50 px-3 py-2"><span class="text-sm text-gray-600">javascript</span><div class="flex items-center gap-2"><button class="flex size-6 items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-md text-gray-400 hover:bg-zinc-200 hover:text-black focus:outline-none"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy size-3.5" aria-hidden="true"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"></rect><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"></path></svg></button></div></div><div class="mt-0 text-sm [&amp;_pre]:py-0 [&amp;_pre]:grid [&amp;_code]:py-4 [&amp;_code]:w-full [&amp;_code]:grid [&amp;_code]:overflow-x-auto [&amp;_code]:no-scrollbar [&amp;_code]:bg-transparent [&amp;_.line]:px-3 [&amp;_.line]:w-full [&amp;_.line]:relative [&amp;_.line]:min-h-5"><div><pre class="shiki github-light" style="background-color:#fff;color:#24292e" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// app.js or server.js in your Express application</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#D73A49">const</span><span style="color:#005CC5"> express</span><span style="color:#D73A49"> =</span><span style="color:#6F42C1"> require</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'express'</span><span style="color:#24292E">);</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#D73A49">const</span><span style="color:#005CC5"> cors</span><span style="color:#D73A49"> =</span><span style="color:#6F42C1"> require</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'cors'</span><span style="color:#24292E">); </span><span style="color:#6A737D">// Make sure you've installed it: npm install cors</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#D73A49">const</span><span style="color:#005CC5"> app</span><span style="color:#D73A49"> =</span><span style="color:#6F42C1"> express</span><span style="color:#24292E">();</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// Configure CORS</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// For development, you might allow all origins:</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// app.use(cors());</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// For production, specify the exact origin of your Netlify front-end</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#D73A49">const</span><span style="color:#005CC5"> allowedOrigins</span><span style="color:#D73A49"> =</span><span style="color:#24292E"> [</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#032F62">  'http://localhost:3000'</span><span style="color:#24292E">, </span><span style="color:#6A737D">// For local front-end development</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#032F62">  'https://your-netlify-app-name.netlify.app'</span><span style="color:#6A737D"> // Your deployed Netlify front-end URL</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">];</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">app.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">use</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">cors</span><span style="color:#24292E">({</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6F42C1">  origin</span><span style="color:#24292E">: </span><span style="color:#D73A49">function</span><span style="color:#24292E"> (</span><span style="color:#E36209">origin</span><span style="color:#24292E">, </span><span style="color:#E36209">callback</span><span style="color:#24292E">) {</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">    // allow requests with no origin (like mobile apps or curl requests)</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#D73A49">    if</span><span style="color:#24292E"> (</span><span style="color:#D73A49">!</span><span style="color:#24292E">origin) </span><span style="color:#D73A49">return</span><span style="color:#6F42C1"> callback</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#005CC5">null</span><span style="color:#24292E">, </span><span style="color:#005CC5">true</span><span style="color:#24292E">);</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#D73A49">    if</span><span style="color:#24292E"> (allowedOrigins.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">indexOf</span><span style="color:#24292E">(origin) </span><span style="color:#D73A49">===</span><span style="color:#D73A49"> -</span><span style="color:#005CC5">1</span><span style="color:#24292E">) {</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#D73A49">      const</span><span style="color:#005CC5"> msg</span><span style="color:#D73A49"> =</span><span style="color:#032F62"> 'The CORS policy for this site does not allow access from the specified Origin.'</span><span style="color:#24292E">;</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#D73A49">      return</span><span style="color:#6F42C1"> callback</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#D73A49">new</span><span style="color:#6F42C1"> Error</span><span style="color:#24292E">(msg), </span><span style="color:#005CC5">false</span><span style="color:#24292E">);</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">    }</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#D73A49">    return</span><span style="color:#6F42C1"> callback</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#005CC5">null</span><span style="color:#24292E">, </span><span style="color:#005CC5">true</span><span style="color:#24292E">);</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">  },</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">  methods: [</span><span style="color:#032F62">'GET'</span><span style="color:#24292E">, </span><span style="color:#032F62">'POST'</span><span style="color:#24292E">, </span><span style="color:#032F62">'PUT'</span><span style="color:#24292E">, </span><span style="color:#032F62">'DELETE'</span><span style="color:#24292E">],</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">  credentials: </span><span style="color:#005CC5">true</span><span style="color:#6A737D"> // If you are sending cookies/authentication headers</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">}));</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">app.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">use</span><span style="color:#24292E">(express.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">json</span><span style="color:#24292E">()); </span><span style="color:#6A737D">// For parsing application/json</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// Your API routes</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// app.use('/api/users', userRoutes);</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// app.use('/api/items', itemRoutes);</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#6A737D">// Simple root route for testing API deployment</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">app.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">get</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'/'</span><span style="color:#24292E">, (</span><span style="color:#E36209">req</span><span style="color:#24292E">, </span><span style="color:#E36209">res</span><span style="color:#24292E">) </span><span style="color:#D73A49">=&gt;</span><span style="color:#24292E"> {</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">    res.</span><span style="color:#6F42C1">send</span><span style="color:#24292E">(</span><span style="color:#032F62">'API is running...'</span><span style="color:#24292E">);</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E">});</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#005CC5">module</span><span style="color:#24292E">.</span><span style="color:#005CC5">exports</span><span style="color:#D73A49"> =</span><span style="color:#24292E"> app; </span><span style="color:#6A737D">// Export app if your server.js uses it</span></span></code></pre></div></div></div>
<p>Remember to install the <code>cors</code> package: <code>npm install cors</code>.</p>
<h2>Exercises and Practice Activities</h2>
<ol>
<li>
<p><strong>Prepare your Full-Stack Application for Deployment:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Front-End:</strong> Navigate to your React front-end project. Run <code>npm run build</code> to ensure your <code>build</code> directory is correctly generated. Inspect the contents of the <code>build</code> folder.</li>
<li><strong>Back-End:</strong>
<ul>
<li>Open your <code>server.js</code> (or equivalent) in your Express back-end project. Modify it to listen on <code>process.env.PORT</code>.</li>
<li>Create a <code>Procfile</code> in the root of your back-end project with the correct command to start your server (e.g., <code>web: node server.js</code>).</li>
<li>Ensure your <code>package.json</code> has a <code>start</code> script and all dependencies are correctly listed.</li>
<li>Configure CORS in your Express app to allow requests from <code>http://localhost:3000</code> (for local testing) and <code>https://&lt;your-netlify-app-name&gt;.netlify.app</code> (you'll get this URL after Netlify deployment).</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Deploy Front-End to Netlify:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Commit your front-end code to a Git repository (e.g., GitHub).</li>
<li>Go to Netlify, sign up or log in, and click "Add new site" -&gt; "Import an existing project".</li>
<li>Connect your Git provider and select your front-end repository.</li>
<li>Configure the build settings:
<ul>
<li><strong>Base directory:</strong> (Leave empty if your front-end is at the root of the repo, or specify <code>frontend/</code> if it's in a subdirectory).</li>
<li><strong>Build command:</strong> <code>npm run build</code></li>
<li><strong>Publish directory:</strong> <code>build</code> (or <code>frontend/build</code> if using a base directory).</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>Click "Deploy site". Once deployed, note down the generated Netlify URL.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Deploy Back-End to Heroku:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Commit your back-end code to a separate Git repository (or a subdirectory within the same repo if you prefer, but often separate repos are cleaner for full-stack).</li>
<li>Install the Heroku CLI if you haven't already.</li>
<li>From your back-end project directory in your terminal:
<ul>
<li><code>heroku login</code></li>
<li><code>heroku create my-unique-api-name</code> (replace <code>my-unique-api-name</code> with a unique name).</li>
<li><code>heroku config:set MONGODB_URI="your_mongodb_atlas_connection_string"</code> (get your connection string from MongoDB Atlas).</li>
<li>Push your code: <code>git add .</code>, <code>git commit -m "Deploy to Heroku"</code>, <code>git push heroku main</code>.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>After deployment, run <code>heroku open</code> to verify your API is running (you should see the "API is running..." message if you added a root route). Note down the Heroku URL.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Connect Deployed Applications:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>In Netlify for your deployed front-end, go to <strong>Site settings &gt; Build &amp; deploy &gt; Environment</strong>.</li>
<li>Add an environment variable:
<ul>
<li><strong>Key:</strong> <code>REACT_APP_API_URL</code></li>
<li><strong>Value:</strong> Your Heroku back-end URL (e.g., <code>https://my-unique-api-name.herokuapp.com</code>)</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>Trigger a new deploy on Netlify (you can usually do this from the "Deploys" section by clicking "Trigger deploy").</li>
<li>Test your full-stack application by navigating to your Netlify front-end URL. Verify that it successfully fetches data from your Heroku back-end and performs any necessary operations.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ol>
  
</div>
